title: Improve errors for missing/invalid API key to reduce onboarding drop-off
author: Dylan Brooks
description: Context: During the Lifecycle Growth Experiments sprint we saw a non-trivial % of first-session failures caused by users attempting a first request without an API key, with the TS SDK surfacing a generic 401/403 or a low-signal fetch error. This PR adds clearer, action-oriented errors for missing/empty keys and invalid/unauthorized keys, including guidance that matches our current onboarding flow (create API key in Console, set env var, retry). What changed: (1) Validate apiKey at client construction time (and before first request) with a dedicated RedwoodAuthError, (2) map 401/403 responses to a RedwoodAuthError with a short remediation message + docs/console links, (3) improve default error text for "Bearer undefined" / empty string cases, (4) update README quickstart snippet to show recommended env var usage, and (5) add unit tests for key edge cases (undefined, empty string, whitespace, revoked key, malformed header). Notes: We intentionally do not log the API key and we avoid echoing request headers in error strings. This is meant to reduce early onboarding frustration and improve activation rate by making the "next best action" explicit. Related: PM-659 onboarding email/console CTA alignment; ENG-10492 activation funnel instrumentation (this reduces noise from accidental auth failures).
commits: sdk: add RedwoodAuthError and missing-key validation
sdk: map 401/403 to actionable auth error messages
docs: update README quickstart to use env var + link to Console API keys
tests: add coverage for missing/empty/invalid api key scenarios
chore: small refactor to error formatting + lint fixes
changed_files: packages/sdk/src/client.ts (validate apiKey; improved request error mapping)
conversation: Marissa Cole (review): The message is much better. Can we make sure the guidance points to the Console path users actually see during onboarding ("API Keys" under Settings) and not an internal URL? Also please keep the copy short enough for in-console surfaced errors (some users paste errors into support).

Dylan Brooks (author): Good call. Updated links to /console/settings/api-keys and shortened the remediation text to 2 sentences + one docs link. Also ensured the error message is stable and doesn’t include request headers.

Nadia Rahman (review): Please double-check that we don’t accidentally emit a new error type that breaks downstream users catching by name/message. Do we expose a stable code property? Suggest adding error.code = "AUTH_MISSING_API_KEY" / "AUTH_INVALID_API_KEY". Also confirm we don’t include the apiKey value anywhere (even truncated).

Dylan Brooks (author): Added `code` field on RedwoodAuthError with `AUTH_MISSING_API_KEY` and `AUTH_INVALID_API_KEY`. Also added a regression test asserting the message does not contain `Authorization` or `Bearer`.

Nikhil Sharma (review): Love the onboarding alignment. One more suggestion: mention the env var name we recommend in docs. People copy/paste snippets. Also for 403 vs 401, the remediation is the same but the phrasing should avoid implying their key is "wrong" if it’s a permissions issue.

Dylan Brooks (author): Updated copy to say "API key is missing or not authorized" for 401/403, and the README snippet now shows `REDWOOD_API_KEY`. Split messages: missing key is explicit; unauthorized suggests checking key + org/project selection in Console.
Marissa Cole (approval): Approved after link/copy changes.
Nadia Rahman (approval): Approved with code field + no-secret assertions.
release_notes: TypeScript SDK now provides actionable errors when API keys are missing/empty or unauthorized (401/403), with stable error codes and updated quickstart guidance.
